2.

The brief facts of the Prosecution case are as follows:
That the marriage of accused No.1 with C.W.1-Ms.Soujanya was solemnized on 25.06.2018 as per Hindu rites and customs and at the time of marriage talks and Soujanya S vs Guruprasad on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131727893/
2 engagement i.e., on 08.03.2018 the accused No.1 to 3 demanded and taken Rs.5,00,000/-cash and during marriage taken gold ornaments like gold chain,
bracelet and finger rings and silver articles as dowry and demanded for a site and car.
The accused No.1 to 3 on 24.06.2018 at the time of reception demanded and received cash of Rs.3,00,000/- from the father of C.W.1 i.e., C.W.4.

After marriage while C.W.1- Smt.Soujanya was residing with the accused persons at the matrimonial home and when C.W.1 was pregnant the accused No.1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 mentally and physically harassed C.W.1 by demanding her to go to work and give her salary to the accused no.1 and also demanded to get a bed, cot, household C.C.14081/2021 articles, mattress and cash of Rs.2,00,000/- and used to abuse her and assaulted her and sent her to her paternal house.

Further on 09.09.2019 when C.W.1 gave birth to a female child the accused No.1 to 4 demanded C.W.1 to get a site registered in her name and Rs. 5,00,000/- cash and when C.W.1 did not agree to the demands of accused No.1 to 4, they left the C.W.1 along with her child at the parental house of C.W.1 and at the parental house Of C.W.1 the accused no.2 and 4 abused C.W.1, 4 and 5 in filthy language and threatened to do away with their life if they did not give dowry as demanded.
The accused No.1 to 6 physically and mentally harassed C.W.1 in the matter of bringing additional dowry.

Thereby accused No.1 to 6 have committed the offences punishable U/Secs.498(A),
504 and 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
3.

On the basis of the Statement of CW-1, the Subramanyanagar police have registered a case under Crime No. 35/2021 for the offences punishable U/s 498(A), 504 and 506 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC and Sec.
3 and 4 of D.P.Act against the accused No.1 to 6 and submitted the FIR before the court.

Thereafter the investigating officer visited the spot and drawn the spot mahazar C.C.14081/2021 and recorded the statement of witnesses on completion of the investigation, the IO has submitted the charge sheet against the accused No.1 to 6 for the offences U/s 498(A), 504 and 506 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
4.
On the appearance of the accused No.1 to 6, the accused No.1 to 6 were enlarged on bail.
The copies of prosecution papers were furnished to the accused No.1 to 6 as contemplated U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both the parties, the charge was framed against the accused No.1 to 6 for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A), 504 and 506 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act and read over to them.
Accused No.1 to 6 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Hence, the matter was posted for evidence.

5. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has got examined one witness as PW-1, out of the total charge sheet witnesses as CW-1 to 13 and got marked five documents as Ex.P1 to P.5.

Since PW-1 who is the material witness has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution and since there is no incriminating evidence against the accused from the material witness itself, no purpose would be served by examining rest of the C.C.14081/2021 witnesses.

Hence, the examination of rest of the witnesses is dropped by rejecting the prayer of the learned Assistant Soujanya S vs Guruprasad on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131727893/
3 Public Prosecutor.
6.

Since PW-1 who is the material witness turned hostile to the case of the prosecution and since there is no incriminating evidence against the accused No.1 to 6 from the material witness, no purpose would be served by issuing summons to rest of the witnesses.
Hence, the evidence of the rest of the witnesses is dropped by rejecting the prayer of the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor.

The statement of the accused No.1 to 6 as required Under Sec.313 of Cr.P.C was dispensed with as there were no incriminating circumstances in the evidence of prosecution witness.
7.

I have heard the arguments addressed by the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor and learned advocate for the accused No.1 to 6.
8.

On going through the facts and circumstances of the prosecution case, the following points would arise for my consideration :
C.C.14081/2021 POINTS 1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 married C.W.1- Ms.Soujanya on 25.06.2018 as per Hindu rites and customs and at the time of marriage the accused No.1 to 3 demanded and taken a total sum of Rs.10 lakhs and gold ornaments for the accused No.1 and silver articles as dowry and thereby the accused No.1 to 6 have committed the offence of "receiving and demanding dowry" punishable U/s 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage while C.W.1- Smt.Soujanya was residing with the accused persons at the matrimonial home and when C.W.1 was pregnant the accused No.1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 mentally and physically harassed C.W.1 by demanding her to go to work and give her salary to the accused no.1 and also demanded to get a bed, cot, household articles, mattress and cash of Rs.2,00,000/- and used to abuse her and assaulted her and sent her to her paternal house.

Further on 09.09.2019 when C.W.1 gave birth to a female child the accused No.1 to 4 demanded C.W.1 to get a site registered in her name and Rs. 5,00,000/- cash and when C.W.1 did not agree to C.C.14081/2021 the demands of accused No.1 to 4, they left the C.W.1 along with her child at the parental house of C.W.1 and at the parental house of C.W.1 and thereby the accused No.1 to 6 have committed the offence of subjecting C.W.1 to cruelty, punishable U/Sec. 498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was residing with the accused No.1 to 6 at the matrimonial home and at the house of C.W.1 the accused No.1 to 6 in the matter of bringing additional dowry abused C.W.1, C.W.4 and 5 in filthy language knowingly that it would give provocation to C.W.1, 4 and 5 to breach public peace and thereby the accused No.1 to 6 have committed the offence of " intentional insult" punishable U/s 504 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?

4 4.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was residing with the accused No.1 to 6 at the matrimonial home and at the house of C.W.1 the accused No.1 to 6 in the matter of bringing additional dowry used to criminally intimidate to the life of C.W.1 for forcing her to bring additional dowry and thereby the accused No.1 to 6 have committed an offence punishable U/s 506 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
C.C.14081/2021 5.

9. My findings to the above Points are as under:
 Point No.1 to 4 : In the Negative.
 Point No.5 :

As per final order,
 For the following: -
 REASONS 10. Point No.1 to 4 :- As these points are inter linked with each other and also similar evidence is led on all these points, I have taken all these points together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and discussion.
10.
It is allegation that the accused No.1 to 6 have committed the offences punishable U/Secs.498(A), 504, 506 r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
In order to prove its case, prosecution has got examined informant of crime/C.W.1 by name Smt.Soujanya as P.W.1.

Out of the documents marked for the prosecution Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.3 is the wedding invitation card, Ex.P.4 are the marriage photos, Ex.P.5 are the receipts for purchase of gold ornaments.

C.C.14081/2021 11. C.W.1/P.W.1 in her chief examination deposed that, accused No.1 is her husband and her marriage with the accused No.1 took place in the year 2018 at Bengaluru and out of wedlock they have a female child.
Initially PW1 supported the case of prosecution in the matter of demand and receipt of dowry and the harassment extended by the accused persons for demanding additional dowry from C.W.1.
The matter was deferred for further chief examination of C.W..1 and on 03.05.2024 the Sr.App submitted no further chief examination of C.W.1.
On 03.05.2024 counsel for accused No.1 to 6 cross examined the witness at length.
During her cross examination P.W.1 being the prime witness turned fully hostile to the case of the prosecution in the lengthy cross-examination made by learned counsel for accused No.l to 6.

The PW1 deposed in her cross examination that the accused persons did not demand and take dowry prior or after the marriage and the accused persons have not physically and mentally harassed her Soujanya S vs Guruprasad on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131727893/
5 and did not threaten her with dire consequences.

She further deposed that she did not lodge complaint against the accused No.1 to 6 and police did not draw mahazar and she does not know the contents of the Ex.P.1 and 2 and further deposed that due to oversight she deposed the evidence against the accused No.1 to 6 C.C.14081/2021 on 18.08.2023.
Nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth to support the case of the prosecution.
During her cross examination by learned APP she deposed that she has compromised the matter with the accused persons.

12. Now on over all perusal of the evidence and prosecution witness as complainant, it is evident to note that P.W.1 being the material witness has not supported the case of prosecution in cross examination made by the counsel for accused No.1 to 6.
The PW-1 prime witness denied the entire case of the prosecution in the cross examination made by Learned Counsel for accused No.1 to 6 and also turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.

The PW1 denied the involvement of the accused No.1 to 6 with regard to physical and mental cruelty and at the out set she has denied the entire case of the prosecution, as she has settled the matter with the accused No.1 to 6.

During the course of her evidence she has not at all stated in respect of subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty and denied the involvement of the accused No.1 to 6 and at the out set she has denied the entire case of the prosecution.
13. However, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor prays to issue summons to other witnesses.

Having considered the facts and C.C.14081/2021 circumstances of this case, this court was of the opinion that even if other witnesses were examined, it would be a futile exercise and no lawful purpose would have been served.

As such examination of the prosecution witnesses only for the purpose of completing the procedural aspect and will not serve any judicial purpose and it is sheer waste of the precious time of the court.
Therefore, the prayer of the learned APP to issue summons to other witnesses was rejected.

At this stage this court relied upon judgment delivered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1996 (3) Crimes 84 Sathish Mehra V/s Delhi Administration & another:
wherein at page No.13 the Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date".

sentences.text: The principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above case is applicable in this case also.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 to 6 beyond all reasonable doubts.

Under these facts and circumstances C.C.14081/2021 of the case, the above Points No.1 to 4 is answered in the 'NEGATIVE'.
14. Point No.5: - In view of the findings of point No.1 to 4 this court proceeds to pass the following;-
Soujanya S vs Guruprasad on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131727893/
6 ORDER
Acting U/Sec.248(1) of Cr.P.C. accused No.1 to 6 are acquitted of the offences punishable U/Secs. 498(A), 504 and 506 r/w Sec. 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
Bail bonds of the accused No.1 to 6 and Surety bond shall stand canceled.
The bail bond executed U/Sec.437(A) of Cr.P.C shall be continued.
